elements.content: Communication Goal: I can describe what is in my bag using 'there is' and 'there are'.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 3. What is it?
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: What's in your bag?
- Materials: Real bags, item cards, bingo sheets, COSYmanuals 'there is/are' and 'plurals' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• describe items inside bags or containers using there is / there are
• distinguish singular and plural items
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles object vocabulary and prepositions from Lesson 9.

Next lesson: Lesson 11 recycles everyday objects to talk about daily use.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

bag — a container for carrying things. Example: My bag is under the desk.
phone — a mobile or telephone. Example: My phone is in my bag.
key — a small object that opens a door. Example: I can't find my key.
wallet — a small case for money and cards. Example: My wallet is in my pocket.
lamp — a light. Example: There is a lamp on the desk.
mirror — glass that shows your reflection. Example: There is a mirror in the bathroom.
book — pages with text or pictures. Example: I read a book every night.
pen — a writing tool. Example: Can I borrow your pen?
room — a space inside a building. Example: My room is small but nice.
table — a piece of furniture with a flat top. Example: The books are on the table.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What's in your bag? (asking about contents)
• There is a phone in my bag. (singular item)
• There are two keys in my bag. (plural items)
• Is there a pen? (yes/no question, singular)
• Are there any books? (yes/no question, plural)
• There isn't a mirror. (negative singular)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a container for carrying things'?
Which word means 'a mobile or telephone'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'there is' and 'there are' to say that something exists or is in a place.

Form:
There is / There are: There is + singular noun. There are + plural noun. Negative: There isn't / There aren't. Question: Is there...? Are there...?

Examples:
• There is a lamp on the desk.
• There are two chairs in the room.
• There isn't a TV in my bedroom.
• Are there any books on the shelf?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ a phone in my bag.
___ three keys on the table.
___ a mirror in the room?
___ any chairs in the kitchen?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• There is ... (a bed / a lamp / a desk) in my room.
• There are ... (two chairs / three books) on the table.
• There isn't ... (a TV / a mirror) in my bedroom.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is in your bag?
• What is in your room?
• Are there any pictures on your wall?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences with 'there is' about your home.
• Write three sentences with 'there are' about your classroom.
Reading: What's in your bag?

What's in your bag? In my bag, there is a phone, a wallet, and a pen. There are two keys and three books. There isn't a mirror. My friend's bag is different. There are two lamps and a big mirror in her room, but there isn't a table. We are ready for school!
How many keys are in the bag?
Is there a mirror in the bag?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What's in your bag?
B: There is a phone and a wallet. There are two keys.
A: Is there a pen?
B: Yes, there is. And there are three books.
A: Are there any snacks?
B: No, there aren't. I'm hungry!
How many keys are in the bag?
Are there any snacks?
Speaking task: Empty your bag on the table. Describe the contents to your partner using 'there is/are'. Then ask about your partner's bag.

• What is always in your bag?
• What is never in your bag?
• How many keys have you got?
• What is in your school bag?
• Which item is the most important?
Role-play: You are at airport security. Open your bag and explain what is inside to the officer.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about what is in your bag.
Model: There is ... There are ... There isn't ... There aren't ...
